title: Chief Herbert D. Proffitt Act of 2025

claims.claim: The Public Safety Officers' Benefits program pays a $250,000 line-of-duty death benefit.
claims.sourceSpan: a benefit of $250,000, adjusted in accordance with subsection (h), and calculated in accordance with subsection (i), shall be payable by the Bureau

claims.claim: The program is run by the Justice Department's Bureau of Justice Assistance.
claims.sourceSpan: the Bureau of Justice Assistance
claims.note: Bureau of Justice Assistance is the administering entity per statute; DOJ parentage confirmed by Findings note ('Department of Justice approved 481 claims').

claims.claim: The death benefit is adjusted each year for inflation.
claims.sourceSpan: to reflect the annual percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
claims.note: Annual CPI adjustment; 'inflation' is a faithful gloss for the CPI mechanism.

claims.claim: The program pays a matching disability benefit (same amount) for permanent and total disability.
claims.sourceSpan: a benefit shall be payable to the public safety officer (if living on the date on which the determination is made) in the same amount that would be payable

claims.claim: The matching disability benefit is paid 'to the families of ... public safety officers ... permanently disabled on the job.'
claims.sourceSpan: a benefit shall be payable to the public safety officer (if living on the date on which the determination is made) in the same amount that would be payable
claims.note: The disability benefit under (b) is payable to the officer if living, not to the family; the summary sentence bundles both death and disability benefits under 'to the families.' Minor recipient imprecision in a compressed summary whose primary subject is the death benefit.

claims.claim: Beneficiaries are the families of police, firefighters, and other public safety officers.
claims.sourceSpan: public safety officers, including police officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, and others

claims.claim: Benefits go to officers killed or permanently disabled on the job (in the line of duty).
claims.sourceSpan: has died as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury sustained in the line of duty

claims.claim: This bill extends the same benefit to retired law enforcement officers who die or become permanently and totally disabled as a direct and proximate result of a targeted attack because of their prior service as an officer.
claims.sourceSpan: A retired law enforcement officer shall be eligible for a benefit under this part if the officer died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack because of the retired law enforcement officer's service as a law enforcement officer

claims.claim: Adds retired law enforcement officers targeted for their prior service to the federal Public Safety Officers' Benefits program.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 1201 of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (34 U.S.C. 10281) is amended by adding at the end the following

claims.claim: Claims apply retroactively to attacks on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any action taken against a retired law enforcement officer described in section 1201(p) of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (as added by this Act) on or after January 1, 2012
claims.note: 'attacks' lightly glosses the statutory 'action taken against'; date and retroactive direction are exact.

claims.claim: $250,000 death benefit.
claims.sourceSpan: a benefit of $250,000, adjusted in accordance with subsection (h), and calculated in accordance with subsection (i), shall be payable by the Bureau

claims.claim: Adjusted each October for inflation.
claims.sourceSpan: On October 1 of each fiscal year beginning after June 1, 1988, the Bureau shall adjust the level of the benefit

claims.claim: Same amount payable for permanent and total disability.
claims.sourceSpan: a benefit shall be payable to the public safety officer (if living on the date on which the determination is made) in the same amount that would be payable

claims.claim: Interim benefit up to $6,000 while a claim is pending.
claims.sourceSpan: the Bureau may make an interim benefit payment not exceeding $6,000, adjusted in accordance with subsection (h)

claims.claim: Covers officers who separated in good standing as a law enforcement officer.
claims.sourceSpan: an individual who separated from service in good standing as a law enforcement officer in an official capacity at a public agency with or without compensation

claims.claim: Trigger: death or permanent total disability from a targeted attack.
claims.sourceSpan: died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack

claims.claim: Attack must be because of the officer's prior law enforcement service.
claims.sourceSpan: because of the retired law enforcement officer's service as a law enforcement officer

claims.claim: Applies to any qualifying attack on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: on or after January 1, 2012

claims.claim: Also covers claims pending before the Bureau of Justice Assistance.
claims.sourceSpan: pending before the Bureau of Justice Assistance or otherwise on the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Takes effect on the date of enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: take effect on the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Adds a new subsection (p) to 34 U.S.C. 10281.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 1201 of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (34 U.S.C. 10281) is amended by adding at the end the following
claims.note: New subsection (p) is the added text; Section 1201 is codified at 34 U.S.C. 10281.

claims.claim: Makes retired law enforcement officers eligible when they die or become permanently and totally disabled from a targeted attack tied to their prior service.
claims.sourceSpan: A retired law enforcement officer shall be eligible for a benefit under this part if the officer died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack because of the retired law enforcement officer's service as a law enforcement officer

claims.claim: A 'retired law enforcement officer' is defined as an individual who separated in good standing as a law enforcement officer in an official capacity at a public agency, with or without compensation.
claims.sourceSpan: an individual who separated from service in good standing as a law enforcement officer in an official capacity at a public agency with or without compensation

claims.claim: Eligibility requires that the death or permanent-and-total disability be the direct and proximate result of a personal injury from a targeted attack because of the officer's service as a law enforcement officer.
claims.sourceSpan: died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack because of the retired law enforcement officer's service as a law enforcement officer

claims.claim: Claims are processed by the Bureau of Justice Assistance under the existing benefits framework.
claims.sourceSpan: pending before the Bureau of Justice Assistance or otherwise on the date of enactment of this Act
claims.note: Bill routes matters through the Bureau of Justice Assistance; the benefit is under the existing part (34 U.S.C. 10281 et seq.).

claims.claim: Sets a retroactive effective date so the new eligibility reaches back to targeted attacks occurring on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any action taken against a retired law enforcement officer described in section 1201(p) of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (as added by this Act) on or after January 1, 2012

claims.claim: The amendments take effect on the date of enactment and apply to any matter pending before the Bureau of Justice Assistance on that date, or filed or accruing after it.
claims.sourceSpan: take effect on the date of enactment of this Act; and (B) apply to any matter-- (i) pending before the Bureau of Justice Assistance or otherwise on the date of enactment of this Act; or (ii) filed (consistent with pre-existing effective dates) or accruing after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: As an exception to that general rule, the amendment applies to any action taken against a retired law enforcement officer on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any action taken against a retired law enforcement officer described in section 1201(p) of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (as added by this Act) on or after January 1, 2012

claims.claim: The provision is Section 2(b)(2) — Exceptions.
claims.sourceSpan: (2) Exceptions.--The amendment made by this section

claims.claim: The bill reaches back nearly 14 years before enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: on or after January 1, 2012
claims.note: Synthesis/arithmetic from the Jan 1 2012 anchor; measured from likely 2025 enactment the span is ~13 years, so 'nearly 14' is a slightly loose characterization (would be accurate only at a 2026 enactment). Non-material.

claims.claim: Applies the new eligibility to any qualifying targeted attack on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: on or after January 1, 2012

claims.claim: The broad retroactivity window is a scope not stated in the bill's short title or Section 2 heading.
claims.sourceSpan: Chief Herbert D. Proffitt Act of 2025
claims.note: Structural observation: neither the short title nor the Sec. 2 heading names the retroactivity; editorial 'underreported' framing, non-material.

claims.claim: The bill does not define 'targeted attack' or list the evidence required to establish that an attack was 'because of' the retiree's prior service.
claims.sourceSpan: died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack
claims.note: Accurate absence: the operative term 'targeted attack' appears without a definition, and no evidentiary standard is stated anywhere in the bill.

claims.claim: The bill applies retroactively to January 1, 2012 but does not set a filing deadline for pre-enactment claims or address prioritization of backlogged retroactive claims.
claims.sourceSpan: on or after January 1, 2012
claims.note: Accurate absence: the bill sets no filing deadline or prioritization rule for pre-enactment claims.

claims.claim: The bill relies on the existing inflation-adjusted death/disability benefit mechanism in 34 U.S.C. 10281 but does not authorize additional appropriations to cover the new class of claims.
claims.sourceSpan: On October 1 of each fiscal year beginning after June 1, 1988, the Bureau shall adjust the level of the benefit
claims.note: Accurate absence: the bill contains no appropriations clause; it hangs the new eligibility on the existing benefit/CPI framework of section 10281.

claims.claim: The bill uses 'retired law enforcement officer' only and does not address whether retired firefighters, emergency medical responders, or other public safety officers qualify.
claims.sourceSpan: an individual who separated from service in good standing as a law enforcement officer in an official capacity at a public agency with or without compensation
claims.note: Accurate absence: the new subsection defines and reaches only 'retired law enforcement officer.'

claims.claim: New subsection 34 U.S.C. 10281(p) — eligibility for retired law enforcement officers who die or become permanently and totally disabled from a targeted attack tied to their prior service.
claims.sourceSpan: A retired law enforcement officer shall be eligible for a benefit under this part if the officer died or became permanently and totally disabled as the direct and proximate result of a personal injury resulting from a targeted attack because of the retired law enforcement officer's service as a law enforcement officer

claims.claim: 34 U.S.C. 10281 is the Public Safety Officers' Death Benefits — Payment of death benefits section.
claims.sourceSpan: Payment of death benefits
claims.note: Section heading 'Payment of death benefits' under Subchapter XI 'Public Safety Officers' Death Benefits.'

claims.claim: Section 10281 is expanded to cover certain retired officers, with retroactive reach to targeted attacks on or after January 1, 2012.
claims.sourceSpan: shall apply to any action taken against a retired law enforcement officer described in section 1201(p) of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 (as added by this Act) on or after January 1, 2012

notes: Short (2,715-char) amendatory bill; program figures ($250,000 death benefit, $6,000 interim benefit, annual CPI adjustment, matching disability benefit) verified against registered referenced source usc-34-10281 (34 U.S.C. 10281). All bill-text claims (new subsection (p) definition + eligibility, targeted-attack trigger, Jan 1 2012 retroactivity, effective date) verified verbatim against the bill. No material issues. Minor: (1) summary phrase 'to the families ... permanently disabled' bundles the disability benefit, which under 10281(b) is payable to the officer if living; (2) 'nearly 14 years' is a slightly loose count from the Jan 1 2012 anchor; (3) 'most likely points of pushback' is analyst forecast framing. Coverage complete for both operative sections; no omissions.
